items.title: Xaluritamig Plus Abiraterone Versus Standard Treatment in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares a new combination therapy (xaluritamig plus abiraterone) against standard treatments for patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who haven't received chemotherapy yet. The study is actively recruiting and measures overall survival as the primary outcome. This represents a novel treatment approach for chemotherapy-naïve mCRPC patients.

items.title: 177Lu-TLX591 Radioligand Therapy Plus Standard Care in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 3 trial tests a radioligand therapy (177Lu-TLX591) combined with standard care versus standard care alone in mCRPC patients who have progressed after androgen receptor pathway inhibitor treatment. The ProstACT Global study is recruiting and evaluates both efficacy and safety. This is a PSMA-targeted radioligand approach for patients with limited options.

items.title: Apalutamide Plus Radiation Guided by PET Imaging After Prostate Surgery
items.summary: This phase 3 trial tests whether adding enhanced therapy (apalutamide with abiraterone and prednisone) to standard radiation and hormone therapy improves outcomes for patients with biochemical recurrence after prostate surgery. A second part tests adding targeted radiation to metastatic sites detected by PET imaging. The trial is recruiting and uses advanced imaging to guide treatment decisions.

items.title: Testosterone Plus ZEN-3694 Followed by Enzalutamide in CRPC
items.summary: This phase 2 trial investigates whether combining testosterone with ZEN-3694 (a BET inhibitor), followed by enzalutamide plus ZEN-3694, can shrink tumors in castration-resistant prostate cancer patients. The study tests a novel approach using testosterone initially to potentially make subsequent therapy more effective. Currently recruiting patients with therapy-resistant disease.

items.title: First-in-Human Study of GSK5471713 in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This early-stage trial evaluates a new drug (GSK5471713) as monotherapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The phase 1/2 study assesses safety, how the drug works in the body, and preliminary effectiveness. Currently recruiting patients to establish the benefit-risk profile of this novel agent.

items.title: GSK5458514 Alone or Combined With Other Therapies in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial evaluates GSK5458514's safety and tolerability in prostate cancer patients, testing the drug alone and in combinations. The study includes dose escalation and expansion phases to determine optimal dosing. Currently recruiting to assess this novel therapeutic approach.

items.title: Olaparib Plus Abiraterone as First-Line Therapy in Chinese Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 3 trial evaluates whether combining olaparib (a PARP inhibitor) with abiraterone improves outcomes compared to abiraterone alone in Chinese patients with metastatic CRPC who haven't received chemotherapy or newer hormone agents. The study is no longer recruiting but continues to follow participants for efficacy and safety data.

items.title: Cognitive Effects of Darolutamide Versus Enzalutamide in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This completed phase 2 trial compared cognitive side effects between darolutamide and enzalutamide in men with metastatic or non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer or metastatic hormone-sensitive disease. The study used validated cognitive testing to measure mental function changes. Results may help guide treatment choices based on cognitive impact.

items.title: Adding Docetaxel to Apalutamide for Non-Responders in Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Disease
items.summary: This phase 3 trial tests whether adding docetaxel chemotherapy benefits metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer patients who don't achieve deep PSA response with initial apalutamide and hormone therapy. The REINFORCE trial is recruiting and uses PSA response to guide treatment intensification decisions.

items.title: Abemaciclib With or Without Atezolizumab for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This completed phase 2 trial tested whether abemaciclib (a targeted chemotherapy) and atezolizumab (an immunotherapy), alone or combined, can shrink or prevent growth of metastatic prostate cancer. The study also evaluated the safety of the combination. Results are available for this molecularly targeted approach.

items.title: ABBV-969 Safety and Effectiveness Study in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 1 trial assesses safety, how the drug moves through the body, and effectiveness of ABBV-969 given intravenously to metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients. The study includes dose escalation and expansion phases with up to 230 participants worldwide. No longer recruiting new patients.

items.title: PSMA-Targeted Radiation Plus Hormone Therapy in Low-Volume Metastatic Disease
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests whether adding 177Lu-PSMA-617 (a radioactive treatment targeting PSMA) to standard hormone therapy, with or without abiraterone, improves outcomes in patients with limited metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The SPARKLE trial is not yet recruiting but offers a novel approach for newly diagnosed or recurrent low-volume disease.

items.title: Tarlatamab for DLL3-Positive Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial investigates whether tarlatamab is effective for DLL3-positive prostate cancer that has spread and either relapsed or not responded to treatment. The study is recruiting patients with this specific biomarker. This represents a novel targeted approach for a subset of aggressive prostate cancers.

items.title: Low Dose Naltrexone for Fatigue in Prostate Cancer Patients
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests whether low-dose naltrexone (3 mg daily pill) can reduce fatigue in men with prostate cancer receiving hormone therapy (ADT) with or without newer hormone medicines. The study is not yet recruiting but addresses a common quality of life issue. This represents a supportive care approach for treatment-related side effects.

items.title: Cediranib Plus Olaparib Versus Olaparib Alone in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 2 trial compares the PARP inhibitor olaparib with or without cediranib (an enzyme blocker) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients. The study is no longer recruiting but continues to follow participants. This combination approach targets DNA repair mechanisms in cancer cells.

items.title: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan Combinations or Monotherapy in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial assesses ifinatamab deruxtecan (an antibody-drug conjugate) alone or combined with other treatments in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is recruiting and evaluates safety, optimal dosing, and PSA response. This represents a novel antibody-based therapeutic approach.

items.title: Darolutamide and Abemaciclib Combination in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This completed phase 1 trial tested the safety and effectiveness of combining abemaciclib with darolutamide and androgen deprivation therapy for metastatic, non-metastatic, and advanced prostate cancers. The study enrolled 93 participants over 6 months of treatment with long-term follow-up. Results are available for this combination approach.

items.title: Mevrometostat With or Without Enzalutamide in CRPC
items.summary: This phase 1 trial evaluates mevrometostat (an epigenetic modifier) alone and combined with enzalutamide in castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who have progressed on prior CRPC treatment. The study is recruiting and includes assessment and maintenance phases. This targets epigenetic mechanisms in resistant disease.

items.title: Different Dosing Schedules of Lutetium-177 PSMA in Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial examines whether lengthening the interval between doses of lutetium-177 PSMA (a radioactive treatment) improves quality of life without reducing survival in hormone-resistant metastatic prostate cancer. The RECIPROCAL trial is recruiting and tests adaptive dosing strategies for this established therapy.

items.title: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan Versus Chemotherapy in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd) to chemotherapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients. The study is recruiting and measures overall survival and time to cancer progression. This represents a potential new standard treatment option for advanced disease.

items.title: Inflammation Pathways Drive Resistance in Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This research review explains how chronic inflammation drives prostate cancer progression and treatment resistance. NFκB and JAK/STAT3 inflammatory pathways interact with androgen receptor signaling to promote tumor survival, growth, immune evasion, and metastasis. Understanding these mechanisms may lead to new treatment strategies targeting inflammation in advanced disease.

items.title: PSMA DNA Vaccine Enhances PD-1 Immunotherapy Against Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This study developed a next-generation DNA vaccine targeting PSMA (a prostate cancer protein) that activates the immune system and improves response to PD-1 checkpoint blockade immunotherapy. In experiments, the vaccine prevented tumor growth and lung metastasis while increasing immune activation. This represents a potential immunotherapy approach for advanced disease.

items.title: New Dual-Target Drug Overcomes c-MYC Resistance in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: Researchers developed a novel drug (compound 21d) that simultaneously blocks BRD4 and AKT pathways to overcome c-MYC-driven resistance in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. AKT inhibitors alone often fail due to c-MYC resistance, but this dual approach addresses both pathways. This represents a new strategy for treatment-resistant disease.

items.title: Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors Show Mixed Results in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This meta-analysis of 21 trials with 1,580 patients evaluated immune checkpoint inhibitors for unselected metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients. One-year survival was 63% and one-year progression-free survival was 17%. Combination therapy with immune checkpoint inhibitors showed better results than single-agent therapy, but overall benefits were modest without biomarker selection.

items.title: New Multi-Biomarker Test for Prostate Cancer Detection Developed
items.summary: Researchers developed a highly sensitive fluorescence-based test that can simultaneously detect PSA and AFP (tumor markers) in a single test well. The technology uses quantum dots linked to antibodies and may enable better early cancer detection through multi-marker testing. This represents an advance in diagnostic technology.

items.title: Zoledronic Acid Protects Bone Health in Metastatic Prostate Cancer Patients
items.summary: This phase 2 trial found that adding zoledronic acid to androgen deprivation therapy plus enzalutamide significantly prevented bone mineral density loss in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer patients. After 18 months, patients not receiving zoledronic acid had significant bone density decreases at the femoral neck and lumbar spine. This supports bone-protective therapy during hormone treatment.
